### Common Tests in a Liver Panel

- **ALT (Alanine transaminase) & AST (Aspartate transaminase):** Enzymes released into the bloodstream when liver cells are stressed or injured. ALT is more specific to the liver, while AST is also found in muscle and other tissues.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdAHEIkXXhirRsKuinyouV8cWHKwnOmTSi0e0_oDk2Zpi1J7ee0wMNrruF41fSGjsHZUZEPcMNaRKOuM6p2PcQmwfotlZtGwAZBU5UVz7pfDnDlPJF5wkSSLrXv1YBn023T9esNLcYSYJynpnZhXCI88qvYV4)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiQEBxCJF1xD9po1MyiWm9w9FsycDmtrzbo3C7yeZUEXRIWGAI84za8nZWcPY4L2Fuyq-AizuVKTs1W0BQx0ne7pv890ZnWlfeSt_MU4zJIq5HDJLHr-W4wK6hu0LbgKxeKgfnPrQMn6rhvMgY6si7Z-lrloObVMVXqKvCvtgGDAr68ttewhqFFY8eA)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESowEBxCJF1yU7SCHaDYOHvuxg2irCPQXe2rLIvft-idkj3r8kqcWo3zROn60jO0Bu8lbGQNo_lZUWPe5lKcbjNHY3QMp_UeMXG7Isn33p_0f3MYc-mr2TibCRNOPjbgaT1igurnFUC1KyWyB46q_8iOVRq3bSkm1b3_AvLyIo6U0q9D-yF6eL2D0eqBwIW_Ub1i70VpvyCexiz30UI5OqH6ZvySTf)
- **ALP (Alkaline phosphatase) & GGT (Gamma-glutamyl transferase):** Enzymes linked to the liver and bile ducts. High levels can point to bile flow issues or bile duct inflammation (ALP is also found in bone).[[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cu0H7L_cYQc&t=3)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdAHEIkXXhirRsKuinyouV8cWHKwnOmTSi0e0_oDk2Zpi1J7ee0wMNrruF41fSGjsHZUZEPcMNaRKOuM6p2PcQmwfotlZtGwAZBU5UVz7pfDnDlPJF5wkSSLrXv1YBn023T9esNLcYSYJynpnZhXCI88qvYV4)
- **Bilirubin:** A waste product from broken-down red blood cells that the liver processes and clears. High levels can cause yellowing of the skin and eyes (jaundice).[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdAHEIkXXhirRsKuinyouV8cWHKwnOmTSi0e0_oDk2Zpi1J7ee0wMNrruF41fSGjsHZUZEPcMNaRKOuM6p2PcQmwfotlZtGwAZBU5UVz7pfDnDlPJF5wkSSLrXv1YBn023T9esNLcYSYJynpnZhXCI88qvYV4)[[2]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cu0H7L_cYQc&t=3)
- **Albumin & Total Protein:** Proteins made largely by the liver that help keep fluid in blood vessels and support overall body functions. Low albumin can signal reduced liver production, malnutrition, or other health issues.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESvgEBxCJF1w_81REEK7M7uz_9GUWMzjnFLrkDbGcpxd7-Lsl4EidK-8Q89HCqmui5WegWt-63wG5qQIvxKFuRmBurlieeFx0CC1JA2Mrbh89yhPrCiRCLTljrAOs7WQCwmgrW9o6v5TC_I4P39H0uVlsJH86eakGruE6rZbRAmin5zKUCAHxQevTH2XLblAdLv003-_0L_kbR3U7AyK2KnuN4GKw5OOnP1XZReNyJaxgpKAf5h_la9ohwaSQ56bUf)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdAHEIkXXhirRsKuinyouV8cWHKwnOmTSi0e0_oDk2Zpi1J7ee0wMNrruF41fSGjsHZUZEPcMNaRKOuM6p2PcQmwfotlZtGwAZBU5UVz7pfDnDlPJF5wkSSLrXv1YBn023T9esNLcYSYJynpnZhXCI88qvYV4)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESowEBxCJF1_jb6R9AX6a_-AQuilUrMKQx7mpQ6lX1RG4782HMFC4ByP2knzIi_qTI3kPJl_UW0DdYZp1L99yrk4OQTwxJPXbhFbCBAZ3-pLLFk9C3kiaJfIZqCUT804DCr8_1PFM3bgohA7UFHiMXc-2mslXe0QdI4_E8t3bSwdurc84bropPYvnC2C0l3YNC05VH4zDQ-z58OOj1hJ8QNXlek0gm)[[4]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=i2PfjEks4GQ&t=3)

### Preparation, Risks, and Interpretation

- **Preparation:** Some labs or combined panels require fasting for several hours beforehand, while others have no fasting requirement. Always confirm instructions with your ordering provider or lab.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESowEBxCJF1yU7SCHaDYOHvuxg2irCPQXe2rLIvft-idkj3r8kqcWo3zROn60jO0Bu8lbGQNo_lZUWPe5lKcbjNHY3QMp_UeMXG7Isn33p_0f3MYc-mr2TibCRNOPjbgaT1igurnFUC1KyWyB46q_8iOVRq3bSkm1b3_AvLyIo6U0q9D-yF6eL2D0eqBwIW_Ub1i70VpvyCexiz30UI5OqH6ZvySTf)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESngEBxCJF1_kyFCxFyfzDUAHqini_lyu87dKGP8ONnjzAbaUMxtpOo-l3Ncq97QIXBXRQpSkx-1QB44w-0f-lmT05RYKOvKrK4ZjYvDwuNxg77uTcBSRwGkXIGDOUHxsJ2EQBmWbNC5PHtImZqLLLQojbJVqDzi6wRdvd28Mv_taVAPn5lNOr6-xvvxJ23zbyKbXi4q7tuOyQK2WrJ9lCgQ)
- **Risks:** LFTs require a standard blood draw. Risks are low and typically limited to brief discomfort or minor bruising at the needle site.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESngEBxCJF1_kyFCxFyfzDUAHqini_lyu87dKGP8ONnjzAbaUMxtpOo-l3Ncq97QIXBXRQpSkx-1QB44w-0f-lmT05RYKOvKrK4ZjYvDwuNxg77uTcBSRwGkXIGDOUHxsJ2EQBmWbNC5PHtImZqLLLQojbJVqDzi6wRdvd28Mv_taVAPn5lNOr6-xvvxJ23zbyKbXi4q7tuOyQK2WrJ9lCgQ)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdAHEIkXXhirRsKuinyouV8cWHKwnOmTSi0e0_oDk2Zpi1J7ee0wMNrruF41fSGjsHZUZEPcMNaRKOuM6p2PcQmwfotlZtGwAZBU5UVz7pfDnDlPJF5wkSSLrXv1YBn023T9esNLcYSYJynpnZhXCI88qvYV4)
- **Interpreting results:** Reference ranges vary slightly by lab, age, and sex. items.title: Preparation, Risks, and Interpretation
items.text: Preparation: Some labs or combined panels require fasting for several hours beforehand, while others have no fasting requirement. Always confirm instructions with your ordering provider or lab. Risks: LFTs require a standard blood draw. Risks are low and typically limited to brief discomfort or minor bruising at the needle site. Interpreting results: Reference ranges vary slightly by lab, age, and sex. Because non-liver factors—such as medications, alcohol use, muscle strain, or other organs—can affect results, abnormal numbers usually prompt follow-up tests, imaging, or repeat checks rather than a standalone diagnosis.
